# Introduction

Introduce the topic and explain why the question matters. Summarize relevant
previous work, identify what your project will add, and cite sources using the
BibTeX entries in `references.bib`.

# Research Questions and Aims

State the main research question and any supporting questions. Explain what
you aim to learn from the data. State hypotheses when they are useful for the
question.

# Data

Identify the data you plan to use. Describe its source, observational unit,
population or scope, time and geographic coverage, key variables, and access or
license conditions. Explain why the data can address your research questions
and note important gaps or limitations.

# Analysis Plan

Describe how you will prepare and explore the data, what summaries,
visualizations, or methods you expect to use, and how the results will address
each research question. Explain how you will check assumptions and evaluate
the limitations of the analysis. Choose methods that fit the question and data.

# Feasibility and Limitations

Identify likely challenges, what additional information or skills you may
need, and how you will adapt if the data or initial analysis does not support
your plan.
